readings.title: Defeat at Ai
readings.subtitle: A Trespass in the Camp
readings.text: [Joshua 7:1] But the children of Yisra’el committed a trespass regarding that which was under the ban, for Aḵan son of Karmi, son of Zaḇdi, son of Zeraḥ, of the tribe of Yehuḏah, took of that which was under the ban. And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against the children of Yisra’el. [1 Chronicles 2:7] And the son of Karmi: Aḵar, the troubler of Yisra’el, who trespassed regarding the thing put under the ban. [Joshua 7:2] And Yehoshua sent men from Yeriḥo to Ai, which is beside Běyth Awen, east of Běyth Ěl, and spoke to them, saying, “Go up and spy out <dn>את</dn> the country.” So the men went up and spied out Ai. [3] And they returned to Yehoshua and said to him, “Do not let all the people go up, but let about two or three thousand men go up and strike <dn>את</dn> Ai. Do not make all the people toil there, for the people of Ai are few.” [4] And about three thousand men went up there from the people, but they fled before the men of Ai. [5] And the men of Ai struck about thirty-six men, for they pursued them from the gate as far as Sheḇarim, and struck them on the descent. And the hearts of the people melted and became like water. [6] And Yehoshua tore his garments, and fell to the earth on his face before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> until evening, he and the elders of Yisra’el, and they put dust on their heads. [7] And Yehoshua said, “Alas, <dn>Master</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, why have <dn>You</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> this people over the Yarden at all – to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? If only we had been content, and dwelt beyond the Yarden! [8] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, what shall I say when Yisra’el turns its back before its enemies? [9] “For the Kenaʽanites and all the inhabitants of the land shall hear, and they shall surround us, and cut off <dn>את</dn> our name from the earth. And what would <dn>You</dn> do for <dn>Your</dn> great Name?” [10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Rise up! Why are you lying on your face?</dq> [11] <dq>“Yisra’el has sinned, and they have also transgressed <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant which <dn>I</dn> commanded them. And they have also taken of that which is under the ban, and have also stolen, and also deceived, and also put it among their own goods.</dq> [12] <dq>“And the children of Yisra’el shall not be able to stand before their enemies. They are going to turn their backs before their enemies, for they have become cursed. <dn>I</dn> am not with you any more, unless you destroy that which is under the ban from your midst.</dq> [13] <dq>“Rise up, set <dn>את</dn> the people apart, and you shall say, ‘Set yourselves apart for tomorrow, for thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el, “That which is under the ban is in your midst, O Yisra’el. You are not able to stand before your enemies until you put away that which is under the ban out of your midst.”</dq> [14] <dq>‘And you shall be brought near in the morning according to your tribes. And it shall be that the tribe which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> takes comes near by clans. And the clan which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> takes comes near by households. And the household which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> takes comes near by men.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And it shall be that he who is taken with that which is under the ban shall be burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed <dn>את</dn> the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and because he has done folly in Yisra’el.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Judgment in the Valley of Achor
readings.subtitle: Purging the Evil
readings.text: [Joshua 7:16] And Yehoshua rose early in the morning and brought <dn>את</dn> Yisra’el near by their tribes, and the tribe of Yehuḏah was taken. [17] And he brought <dn>את</dn> the clan of Yehuḏah near, and <dn>He</dn> took <dn>את</dn> the clan of the Zarḥites. And he brought <dn>את</dn> the clan of the Zarḥites near by men, and Zaḇdi was taken. [18] And he brought <dn>את</dn> his household near by men, and Aḵan son of Karmi, son of Zaḇdi, son of Zeraḥ, of the tribe of Yehuḏah, was taken. [19] And Yehoshua said to Aḵan, “My son, please give esteem to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el, and make confession to <dn>Him</dn>, and please tell me what you have done – do not hide it from me.” [20] And Aḵan answered Yehoshua and said, “Truly I have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el, and this is what I did: [21] “When I saw among the spoil a lovely garment from Shinʽar, and two hundred sheqels of silver, and a wedge of gold weighing fifty sheqels, I lusted after them and took them. And see, they are hidden in the earth in the midst of my tent, with the silver under it.” [22] And Yehoshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. And see, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver under it. [23] And they took them from the midst of the tent, and brought them to Yehoshua and to all the children of Yisra’el, and laid them out before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [24] And Yehoshua, and all Yisra’el with him, took <dn>את</dn> Aḵan son of Zeraḥ, and <dn>את</dn> the silver, and <dn>את</dn> the garment, and <dn>את</dn> the wedge of gold, and <dn>את</dn> his sons, and <dn>את</dn> his daughters, and <dn>את</dn> his cattle, and <dn>את</dn> his donkeys, and <dn>את</dn> his sheep, and <dn>את</dn> his tent, and <dn>את</dn> all that he had, and they brought them to the Valley of Aḵor. [25] And Yehoshua said, “Why have you troubled us? <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> troubles you this day!” And all Yisra’el stoned <dn>את</dn> him with stones. And they burned <dn>את</dn> them with fire after they had stoned <dn>את</dn> them with stones. [26] And they raised over him a great heap of stones, which remains to this day. Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turned from the heat of <dn>His</dn> displeasure. Therefore the name of that place has been called the Valley of Aḵor to this day.

readings.title: Victory at Ai
readings.subtitle: Ambush and Conquest
readings.text: [Joshua 8:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Do not be afraid, nor be discouraged. Take all the people of war with you, and arise, go up to Ai. See, <dn>I</dn> have given into your hand <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ai, and <dn>את</dn> his people, and <dn>את</dn> his city, and <dn>את</dn> his land.</dq> [2] <dq>“And you shall do to Ai and its sovereign as you did to Yeriḥo and its sovereign. Only its spoil and its livestock you take as plunder for yourselves. Lay an ambush for the city behind it.”</dq> [3] And Yehoshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up against Ai. And Yehoshua chose thirty thousand mighty men of valour and sent them away by night. [4] And he commanded them, saying, “Look, you are going to lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, but all of you be ready. [5] “And I and all the people who are with me shall approach the city. And it shall be, when they come out against us as at the first, that we shall flee before them. [6] “And they shall come out after us till we have drawn them from the city, for they say, ‘They are fleeing before us as at the first.’ And we shall flee before them. [7] “And you shall rise from the ambush and seize the city, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall give it into your hand. [8] “And it shall be, when you have taken <dn>את</dn> the city, that you set <dn>את</dn> the city on fire. Do according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Look, I have commanded you.” [9] And Yehoshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush, and stayed between Běyth Ěl and Ai, on the west side of Ai. But Yehoshua stayed that night in the midst of the people. [10] And Yehoshua rose early in the morning and inspected <dn>את</dn> the people, and went up, he and the elders of Yisra’el, before the people to Ai. [11] And all the people of war who were with him went up and drew near. And they came before the city and camped on the north side of Ai, and a valley was between them and Ai. [12] And he took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Běyth Ěl and Ai, on the west side of the city. [13] And when they had set <dn>את</dn> the people, <dn>את</dn> all the army that was on the north of the city, and its rear guard on the west of the city, Yehoshua went that night into the midst of the valley. [14] And it came to be, when the sovereign of Ai saw it, that the men of the city hastened and rose early and went out against Yisra’el to battle, he and all his people, at an appointed place before the desert plain. But he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city. [15] And Yehoshua and all Yisra’el let themselves be beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness. [16] And all the people who were in Ai were called together to pursue them. And they pursued Yehoshua and were drawn away from the city. [17] And there was not a man left in Ai or Běyth Ěl who did not go out after Yisra’el. So they left <dn>את</dn> the city open and pursued Yisra’el. [18] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Stretch out the spear that is in your hand toward Ai, for <dn>I</dn> give it into your hand.”</dq> And Yehoshua stretched out the spear that was in his hand toward the city. [19] And those in ambush rose quickly from their place. And they ran as soon as he had stretched out his hand, and they entered the city and took it, and hastened to set <dn>את</dn> the city on fire. [20] And the men of Ai looked behind them and saw, and look, the smoke of the city ascended to the heavens. And they had no power to flee this way or that way, and the people who had fled to the wilderness turned back on the pursuers. [21] And when Yehoshua and all Yisra’el saw that the ambush had captured <dn>את</dn> the city, and that the smoke of the city ascended, they turned back and struck <dn>את</dn> the men of Ai. [22] And the others came out of the city against them, so they were in the midst of Yisra’el, some on this side and some on that side. And they struck them until there was not left to them a survivor or fugitive. [23] And they caught <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ai alive, and brought <dn>את</dn> him to Yehoshua. [24] And it came to be, when Yisra’el had ended slaying <dn>את</dn> all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness where they pursued them, and when they all had fallen by the edge of the sword until they were consumed, that all Yisra’el returned to Ai and struck <dn>את</dn> it with the edge of the sword. [25] And it came to be that all who fell that day, both men and women, were twelve thousand – all the people of Ai. [26] And Yehoshua did not withdraw his hand with which he stretched out the spear until he had completely destroyed <dn>את</dn> all the inhabitants of Ai. [27] Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Yisra’el took as booty for themselves, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua. [28] And Yehoshua burned <dn>את</dn> Ai and made it a heap forever, a ruin to this day. [29] And he hanged <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ai on a tree until evening. And at sundown Yehoshua commanded that they should take <dn>את</dn> his corpse down from the tree, cast it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raise over it a great heap of stones that remains to this day.

readings.title: Renewal of the Covenant
readings.subtitle: Blessings and Curses at Mount Ebal
readings.text: [Joshua 8:30] Then Yehoshua built an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el in Mount Ěyḇal, [31] as Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’el, as it is written in the Book of the Torah of Mosheh, “an altar of unhewn stones over which no man has wielded iron.” And they offered on it burnt offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and sacrificed peace offerings. [32] And there, in the presence of the children of Yisra’el, he wrote on the stones <dn>את</dn> a copy of the Torah of Mosheh, which he had written. [33] And all Yisra’el, with their elders and officers and judges, stood on either side of the ark before the priests, the Lewites, who bore the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the stranger as well as the native. Half of them were in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ěyḇal, as Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded before, that they should bless <dn>את</dn> the people of Yisra’el. [34] And afterward he read <dn>את</dn> all the words of the Torah, the blessings and the cursings, according to all that is written in the Book of the Torah. [35] There was not a word of all that Mosheh had commanded which Yehoshua did not read before all the assembly of Yisra’el, with the women, the little ones, and the strangers who walked among them. [Joshua 9:1] And it came to be when all the sovereigns who were beyond the Yarden, in the mountains and in the lowlands and along all the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanono – the Ḥittite, the Amorite, the Kenaʽanite, the Perizzite, the Ḥiwwite, and the Yeḇusite – heard about it, [2] that they gathered together to fight with Yehoshua and Yisra’el with one mouth. [3] And the inhabitants of Giḇʽon heard what Yehoshua had done to Yeriḥo and Ai, [4] and they also acted craftily, and went and pretended to be ambassadors. And they took old sacks on their donkeys, and old wineskins torn and mended, [5] and old and patched sandals on their feet, and old garments on themselves. And all the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy. [6] And they went to Yehoshua, to the camp at Gilgal, and said to him and to the men of Yisra’el, “We have come from a far land. And now, make a covenant with us.” [7] But the men of Yisra’el said to the Ḥiwwites, “Perhaps you dwell in our midst, so how shall we make a covenant with you?” [8] And they said to Yehoshua, “We are your servants.” And Yehoshua said to them, “Who are you, and where do you come from?” [9] And they said to him, “From a very far land your servants have come because of the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. For we have heard of <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> report, and all that <dn>He</dn> did in Mitsrayim, [10] and all that <dn>He</dn> did to the two sovereigns of the Amorites who were beyond the Yarden, to Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon, and to Og sovereign of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth. [11] “So our elders and all the inhabitants of our country spoke to us, saying, ‘Take provisions with you for the journey, and go to meet them, and say to them, “We are your servants, and now make a covenant with us.” ’ [12] “This bread of ours we took hot for our provision from our houses on the day we left to come to you, but now look, it is dry and mouldy. [13] “And these wineskins which we filled were new, and see, they are torn. And these our garments and our sandals have become old because of the very long journey.” [14] And the men took some of their provisions, but they did not ask <dn>את</dn> the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] So Yehoshua made peace with them, and made a covenant with them to let them live. And the rulers of the congregation swore to them. [16] And it came to be at the end of three days, after they had made a covenant with them, that they heard that they were their neighbours who dwelt near them. [17] And the children of Yisra’el set out and came to their cities on the third day. Now their cities were Giḇʽon, and Kephirah, and Be’ěroth, and Qiryath Yeʽarim. [18] But the children of Yisra’el did not strike them, because the rulers of the congregation had sworn to them by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el. And all the congregation grumbled against the rulers. [19] And all the rulers said to all the congregation, “We have sworn to them by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el, and now we are unable to touch them. [20] “This we do to them: We shall let them live, lest wrath be upon us because of the oath which we swore to them.” [21] And the rulers said to them, “Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and water drawers for all the congregation, as the rulers had promised them.” [22] And Yehoshua called for them, and he spoke to them, saying, “Why have you deceived us, saying, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you dwell in our midst? [23] “And now you are cursed, and none of you is freed from being slaves – woodcutters and water drawers for the house of my <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [24] And they answered Yehoshua and said, “Because your servants were clearly told that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> servant Mosheh to give you <dn>את</dn> all the land, and to destroy <dn>את</dn> all the inhabitants of the land from before you. So we were very much afraid for our lives because of you, and have done this deed. [25] “And now, see, we are in your hand. Do with us as it seems good and right in your eyes to do.” [26] And he did so to them, and delivered <dn>את</dn> them out of the hand of the children of Yisra’el, so that they did not kill them. [27] And that day Yehoshua made them woodcutters and water drawers for the congregation and for the altar of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, even to this day, in the place which <dn>He</dn> would choose.
